general_disclaimer: Requirements can vary according to the person's circumstances, age, citizenship, family situation, and the reason for the application. Home Affairs may request additional documents after reviewing a case.

birth_registration.intro: A birth should be registered within 30 days of the child's birth. The application is made by a parent, next of kin, or legal guardian at a Home Affairs office. If the child was born outside South Africa, registration may be handled through a South African embassy or consulate.

cost.note: The first birth registration and first birth certificate are generally free. Do not add a certificate re-issue fee to a first birth-registration checklist.

general_requirements.personal_attendance: The parent, guardian, or informant must attend where Home Affairs needs to verify the application.
general_requirements.biometrics: The child may need to be present for biometric capture (palm, footprint, or fingerprint), depending on age and the specific registration.

base_documents.issuer: Hospital, clinic, or other health facility
base_documents.note: Confirms the birth; normally completed or issued through the health facility where the child was born.
Provide original documents or certified copies where requested.

base_documents.applies_when: relevant to the registration (e.g. the parents are married)
base_documents.note: Required where relevant to the registration. Not normally issued afresh for the birth-registration application.

birth_outside_health_facility.trigger_label: The birth happened outside a health facility

documents.issuer: Home Affairs provides the form; the person who witnessed the birth supplies the information
documents.note: Required where the birth occurred outside a health facility. The form is obtained from a Home Affairs office.

parents_unmarried_father_to_be_recorded.trigger_label: Parents are unmarried and the father is to be recorded

documents.issuer: Home Affairs, completed by the relevant parents
documents.note: May be required where the parents are unmarried and the father is to be recorded. Both parents may need to appear.

child_abandoned_orphaned_or_disputed_par.trigger_label: Child is abandoned or orphaned, parentage is disputed, or another exceptional guardianship situation applies

documents.issuer: Relevant magistrates' or High Court, depending on the matter
documents.note: May be required for an abandoned or orphaned child, disputed parentage, guardianship, or another exceptional situation.

registered_by_someone_other_than_a_paren.trigger_label: Someone other than a parent (guardian, next of kin, other authorised informant) is registering the birth

documents.issuer: The legal guardian, next of kin, or other authorised informant
documents.note: Required where someone other than a parent registers the birth.
May be required where a guardian, social worker, or institution is acting for the child.

late_registration.label: Registering more than 30 days after the birth
late_registration.message: Late registration is a different process and can require additional evidence, interviews, affidavits, verification, or approval. I don't have the specific document checklist for late registration — please confirm the requirements with your nearest Home Affairs office.

smart_id.intro: A branch visit or approved biometric channel is generally required for photograph, fingerprints, and signature. eHomeAffairs can support an online application for eligible applicants, but it does not eliminate biometric capture.

first_application_16_plus.label: First Smart ID application — applicant aged 16 or older
first_application_16_plus.cost_note: No fee is stated in the source material for a first application. Confirm with Home Affairs.

general_requirements.biometrics: Photograph, fingerprints, and signature, captured at a branch or approved biometric channel.

base_documents.issuer: Home Affairs or the applicant's existing records
base_documents.note: A certified copy may be required.

base_documents.document: Parent, legal guardian, or informant's ID
base_documents.issuer: The relevant parent, guardian, or informant
base_documents.note: Home Affairs' Smart ID requirements refer to a certified copy.

base_documents.applies_when: the applicant already has an ID book or another identity document
base_documents.note: Required if the person already has an ID book or another identity document.

base_documents.issuer: Captured by Home Affairs or an approved partner

documents.issuer: Home Affairs or the family's existing records
documents.note: May be required where a parent is deceased.

documents.issuer: Home Affairs or the family's existing records
documents.note: May be required where a parent is deceased.

guardian_acting_for_applicant.trigger_label: A legal guardian is acting for the applicant

documents.note: Required where a legal guardian is acting for the applicant.

renewal_or_replacement.label: Renewal or replacement of an existing ID / Smart ID
renewal_or_replacement.intro: First establish which situation applies: replacing a green ID book with a Smart ID, replacing a Smart ID, a lost/stolen document, a minor applicant, a parent-deceased case, a marital-status change, or a pending name/surname amendment.

cost.amount: R140 re-issue fee (published Home Affairs guidance, for the relevant re-issue category)
cost.note: Fees should still be verified before implementation because tariffs can change.

replacing_green_id_book.label: Replacing a green ID book with a Smart ID

documents.document: Existing green ID book or a copy

book_lost.trigger_label: The green ID book is lost

documents.note: If lost, an affidavit may be required.

card_lost_or_damaged.trigger_label: The Smart ID is lost or damaged

documents.note: If lost or damaged, an affidavit or other loss/damage documentation may be required.

documents.applies_when: where required by the office or application channel
documents.note: Where required by the office or application channel.
The deceased parent's identity evidence, where required.

documents.document: Marriage certificate or other relevant legal document
documents.issuer: Home Affairs / the applicant's existing records

name_or_surname_amendment_pending.label: Name or surname amendment
name_or_surname_amendment_pending.process_note: The amendment must generally be finalised before a new Smart ID is issued.

important_exclusions: Do not tell every applicant to obtain a new birth certificate.
Do not tell every applicant to complete one universal BI-9 form — there is no single universal Smart ID form for every case.
Do not tell every applicant to pay a fixed birth-certificate fee.
Do not tell every applicant to bring a parent's ID regardless of age or application type.
The correct requirements depend on the application pathway and the applicant's circumstances.

passport.intro: Passport applications can be initiated through eHomeAffairs or submitted through an eligible Home Affairs office, participating bank, or South African mission abroad. The applicant must still meet biometric and document requirements.

cost.note: Paid through the relevant application channel. Verify before the demo because tariffs may change.

base_documents.issuer: Home Affairs office or application channel
base_documents.note: This is the passport application form.

base_documents.document: Original South African ID and copy
base_documents.note: Required for an adult South African citizen.
Present it if renewing or replacing a passport.
Not needed at Smart ID card offices where the image is captured digitally.

passport_lost_or_stolen.trigger_label: The passport was lost or stolen

documents.document: Loss report, Form DHA-335, and police affidavit
documents.issuer: Home Affairs provides the loss-report form; SAPS records the loss
documents.note: Required if the passport was lost or stolen.

cost.note: The prescribed fee applies; the amount is not stated for this category in the source material — confirm with Home Affairs.

base_documents.note: Provided instead of an ID.
Parental consent and attendance where required.
If renewing.
Unless digital capture is available.
Parental consent is required for the issue of a passport.
Both parents may need to provide their IDs, especially where both parents appear on the birth certificate.

base_documents.document: Child's original or certified birth certificate
base_documents.note: Especially where both parents appear on the birth certificate.

documents.document: Consent, affidavit, court order, or other evidence explaining the parent's absence
documents.issuer: Varies — Home Affairs / commissioner of oaths / court, depending on which is used
documents.note: If one parent is unavailable, Home Affairs may require consent, an affidavit, a court order, or other evidence explaining the absence.

applying_abroad.label: Applying from outside South Africa

cost.note: Photographs and payment are required; the amount depends on the application channel/mission — confirm with the relevant South African mission.

base_documents.document: Existing ID, passport, or birth record

base_documents.note: Form DHA-529 for determination of citizenship where required.

base_documents.document: Supporting documents requested by the embassy or consulate

process_notes: The overseas mission may have additional appointment and document rules.

name_surname_amendment.intro: Name and surname applications are not one single process. The documents depend on whether the issue is a spelling error, marriage, divorce, widowhood, a child's surname, adoption, parentage, or an adult choosing an unrelated surname. Home Affairs' amendment services include altering a forename, changing a minor's surname, assuming a different surname, and correcting information such as date or place of birth.

spelling_error.label: Spelling or administrative error

base_documents.document: Documentary proof showing the correct spelling
Certified copies of relevant parent or family records

base_documents.note: For applicants aged 16 or older.

example_supporting_evidence: Parent's ID with the correct spelling
Applicant's school, medical, or official records
Death or marriage certificates showing the correct family surname
spelling_error.disclaimer: Home Affairs may require additional evidence if the correction affects parentage, citizenship, or the underlying birth record.

marriage.label: Marriage-related surname change

base_documents.issuer: Home Affairs, if the marriage was registered there
base_documents.note: If the applicant already holds the certificate, the original or certified copy should be supplied.

base_documents.document: Written confirmation of the surname the applicant wishes to use

process_notes: A new Smart ID or passport application is needed after the marital change is recorded.

base_documents.applies_when: where needed to link the records

base_documents.document: Written confirmation of the surname the applicant wants to resume or use

documents.issuer: The court that granted the divorce

documents.document: Death certificate of the deceased spouse
documents.note: Can be requested from Home Affairs if the family does not have the original.

child_surname.label: Changing a child's surname

base_documents.document: IDs of the parents or legal guardians
Written consent of the natural parents
A good and sufficient written reason for the change

taking_stepparent_surname.trigger_label: The child is taking a stepparent's surname

follows_parents_marriage.trigger_label: The change follows the parents' marriage

guardianship_or_adoption.trigger_label: The application relates to guardianship or adoption

consent_unavailable_disputed_or_court_de.trigger_label: Parental consent is unavailable, disputed, or replaced by a court decision

documents.note: Where consent is unavailable, disputed, or replaced by a court decision.

process_notes: Home Affairs' published amendment guidance refers to parental consent, marriage certificates, certified identity documents, affidavits, and online verification results for relevant child-surname cases.

adult_unrelated_surname.label: Adult assuming an unrelated surname

base_documents.note: Potentially including a full or unabridged record where required.

base_documents.document: Evidence of the surname's family or legal connection
Supporting family marriage, birth, or death certificates
Any additional forms specified by Home Affairs

surname_holder_consent_relevant.trigger_label: Consent from the surname holder is relevant

documents.document: Certified copy of the surname holder's ID

adult_unrelated_surname.disclaimer: This is usually more complex than correcting a spelling error. The application should not promise approval — Home Affairs must investigate and decide whether the evidence supports the change.
